description: Does an atomic System One battery composed by explicit, non-compensatory code decide whether a Planning contract is ready for dispatch, compared with the historical holistic judgment and with the incumbent deterministic readiness state?
falsification_criteria: The explicit atomic policy is no better than the holistic arm on the test partition: the paired false-READY difference's 95% interval contains zero.
At least one mutation class leaves its declared primitive statistically unmoved, or moves unrelated primitives as much as the declared one.
hypothesis: Atomic System One judgments composed by an explicit non-compensatory policy separate genuinely ready contracts from not-ready ones with a lower false-READY rate than the historical holistic judgment, and each primitive moves in the expected direction under a controlled mutation of the invariant it names.

non_claims: No production or runtime adoption of System One readiness is claimed: Substrate readiness stays deterministic plus attestation until a benchmark supports more.
No claim about the joint correctness of the incumbent's own readiness state: it is a baseline, not an oracle.
No claim that a semantic judgment replaces a deterministic check: structure is checked by code.
No claim about downstream dispatch outcomes beyond the closure/supersession evidence available on the frozen board snapshot.
research_question: Can atomic System One judgments over a Planning work contract, composed by explicit code, decide READY / DRAFT / NEEDS_DECISION / BLOCKED / REVIEW as well as or better than the historical single holistic 'executable' judgment, and what does each primitive actually measure?
success_criteria: On the frozen test partition, the explicit atomic policy's false-READY rate is lower than the holistic arm's, with the paired difference's 95% interval excluding zero, and inflated neither by the easy structurally-invalid pool (excluded by construction) nor by escalation.
Every mutation class moves its declared primitive in the declared direction with a 95% interval excluding zero, while no unrelated primitive moves without an explanation.

terminology.Choice: Selection of one option from a defined set, returned with probabilities and a confidence that describes the shape of the distribution.
terminology.Jev: The TypeSafe System One model this experiment calls, requested as the alias jev-latest and recorded with its resolved version.
terminology.Noul: P(yes) for a yes/no question. There is no separate confidence field: 0.5 means yes and no are similarly likely, not 'medium'.
terminology.Score: A probability-weighted position on an ordered legend. Not used by this experiment: the Ready contract has no ordinal dimension.
terminology.System One: A TypeSafe model interface evaluating atomic questions over supplied state and returning typed probabilistic answers. It owns no control flow and performs no side effects.
terminology.deterministic channel: Facts code can prove exactly (required sections, unresolved markers, referenced artifacts). Never asked of a System One model.
terminology.incumbent readiness: Substrate's current readiness state: deterministic structural validation plus an explicit human/policy attestation per revision.
